title: 生涯学習特別科目(国際協力論)
subtitle: Special Subject - Lifelong Learning (Theory of International Cooperation)
courseType:
(Provided by all courses)
Liberal Arts Courses
Transdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal: Recently, there are variety of approaches for international cooperation, even in people's daily life. In this course, students will learn that people are able to participate in supporting developing countries and the poor in many ways. Students are expected to understand such current situation. Upon completing this course, students will be able to think by themselves how to contribute to international cooperation.
advice: (Outline of the course) Students will learn activities of development assistance cooperation, international organizations, or NGO to support other people living inside and outside of their countries through learning international affairs. The goal of the students is to achieve the basic knowledge of international cooperation and its background so that they can practice such activities in their future. Students will learn the concept of international/global development/cooperation and its practice. By the end of the course, students will learn K (Kindness of Heart), I (Intellectual Curiosity), T (Team Sprits), So that they can acquire skills and knowledges that they can practice in future. (Advice and comments) 1)Students will learn to open up their eyes to watch the world, to take interests in social issues, and keep their minds on such issues. 2)The international and social issues which will be discussed in these classes will be the issues that students may have to tackle in future. 3)The program of the course may change depending on the number of students and circumstances of classes. 4)A lecturer of one class will be a guest lecturer from outside, so there may be some changes in the program. 5)The lecturer of this course used to work for JBIC and JICA, as well as served as a JOCV, and as a director of an NGO.
books: 1)David, Hulme, 2016, Should Rich Nations Help the Poor?, Polity press 2)Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA), every year, White Paper on Development Cooperation / Japan's ODA White Paper, MOFA: https://www.mofa.go.jp/policy/oda/page_000017.html 3)Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), every year, JICA Annual Report, JICA: https://www.jica.go.jp/english/about/disc/report/index.html
requiredKnowledge: No specific requirements to take this course. It is desirable that students have interests in daily international issues. Some English materials will be used.

activityGoals.body: Discuss and argue whether and why international cooperation is necessary.
Comprehend and explain the roles and needs of Official Development Assistance (ODA) .
Understand and explain approaches by the government level, the grass-root level, and the private sector level.
Analyze the trends of international cooperation at global level in relation with global society.
Plan his/her own roles/actions to contribute to international cooperation.
Express his/her own critical view about international cooperation and/or ODA.

achievementLevels.ideal: 1) Acquire methods and approaches to analyze and discuss about developing countries, global south, poverty, from academic and multi-disciplinary aspects. 2) Understand historical and ideological background on international development to fight against poverty through the process in 1) above. 3) Gain skills and knowledge to discuss and take actions in his/her career in future to support international cooperation.
achievementLevels.standard: 1) Learn about "developing countries", "global south", "poverty" and so on as common knowledge. 2) Understand about the historical background about international cooperation to fight against poverty. 3) Think about what s/he can do in his/her career to do something for international cooperation.

lessons.content: Introduction of lecturer Guidance of the course Requests from students.
Learning about international cooperation through the career of the lecturer (JOCV, IDEAS, IDPM. JBIC, JICA). To learn about what can be done.
Nations all over the world: OECD, Asia, Africa, Latin America, Middle East To learn about the world.
International Cooperation, ODA, Japanese ODA To learn what international cooperation and ODA means.
Activities of Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) To learn the roles and functions of JICA, which is the main ODA executing agency in Japan.
JICA Volunteer program To learn about the most famous JICA program, such as its functions, process, purposes, achievements etc.
Learning from an experiece of a JOCV (lecturer or another ex-JOCV) Listen to actual, real voice of ex-JOCV to learn what can be done.
Learning from Video of JOCV Watch videos and discuss about the possibilities and difficulties of JOCV.
Introduction to NGO Learn about the role of NGO, which is representing civil society. (Some portions of this class overlap with "Theory of NGO")
Introduction to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) Learn about the background, the history, the meaning of SDGs.
SDGs Workshop (Group work) Re-arranging the order of SDGs: Students will discuss and re-organize the order of SDGs in groups according to their priorities (with reasons).
lessons.operation: Lecture and exercise Discussion Group work

lessons.content: Private sectors' social role Learning the roles of private sectors and its background in international cooperation.
lessons.assignments: Review Reaction paper Preview Report No.1 on JOCV

lessons.content: "Should Rich Nations Help the Poor?" Learning the reason why we have to help the poor through a masterpiece book. A group work is also required.
lessons.operation: Lecture and exercise Discussion Group work

lessons.content: Disability and Development Learning the actual situation and possibility in supporting persons with disabilities in developing countries.
lessons.assignments: Review Reaction paper Preview Report No.2

lessons.content: Review the whole course (wrapping-up, reviewing the scores, and conducting self-inspections). Reconsider what students can learn in this course.
